name: Technical Writing Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in technical writing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in technical writing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting technical writing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. State assumptions about technical writing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
3. Prefer explicit, readable technical writing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. When technical writing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Validate technical writing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to technical writing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen technical writing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. Keep technical writing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
9. Check that technical writing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
10. When technical writing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
11. Keep technical writing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting technical writing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic technical writing advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of technical writing correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated technical writing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these technical writing guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
